$comment: Extraction vectors for the JSONPath subset in spec/04-expression-language.md#extraction--a-jsonpath-subset. Every runtime's extraction implementation must match every case here exactly, including the missing-path cases: `missing: true` means the runtime's result for this path must be the explicit missing-value the runtime uses internally to mean 'did not resolve': never null coerced to a value, never an empty string, never a thrown error for extraction itself (a step that requires the value to resolve fails at the point it's used, not at extraction). `invalid: true` is a distinct marker from `missing: true`: it means the path string itself is not well-formed grammar (e.g. no navigation segment at all), which a runtime may reject earlier (at manifest-load or validate time) rather than at extraction time, whereas a `missing: true` path is grammatically valid but does not resolve against this particular document.

cases.description: top-level field
nested field, two levels
nested field, three levels
array index access, object element
array index access, numeric field
wildcard projection over array of objects, string field
wildcard projection over array of objects, numeric field
missing top-level field
missing nested field
array index out of range
path continues through a null intermediate value
path continues through a non-existent intermediate object
wildcard over a non-existent array yields missing, not an empty array
boolean field value, distinct from a string "true"
zero is a resolved value, not missing
null is a resolved value in its own right when it is the leaf, distinct from a missing/absent path
single-element array, index 0
wildcard projection over a single-element array still yields a one-element array, not the bare scalar
wildcard projection over an empty array yields an empty array, a resolved value distinct from the missing-array case above
negative array index is not supported by this grammar; treated as an unresolved path, never Python-style from-the-end indexing
nested array-of-arrays, first level index only (no [i][j] chaining in this grammar)
field access attempted on a scalar (not an object) fails to resolve, not a type error
array index attempted on a non-array field fails to resolve
wildcard attempted on a non-array field fails to resolve

bare $ with no further segments is not a valid path at all (the grammar requires at least one .field or [index] segment; see schema/manifest.v1.schema.json's status_map.path pattern), distinct from a path that resolves to missing
cases.why: Every real use of an extraction path (status_map.path, errors[].match.path, ${extract...} interpolation) requires navigating to a specific field; a runtime should treat a bare $ the same as any other malformed path, not as a request for the whole document.

cases.description: wildcard projecting a field that is itself present-but-null on every element yields an array of nulls, not missing
cases.why: Every element of data.items lacks this field entirely (not merely null), so the wildcard projection itself fails to resolve rather than yielding [null, null]; contrast with the single-element null-leaf case above, where the field is present with a null value.
